editorial.headline: Live-Animal Wholesale: Nationally Open, Bali-Blocked for PMA
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet PMA registration is blocked across Bali under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the wholesale trade of live animals other than fish, including poultry, slaughter livestock and breeding animals. Its centre of gravity is commerce in living stock: an enterprise registered here is dealing at wholesale level in those animals, rather than operating within an undefined adjacent activity. The scope is deliberately broad enough to include both animals intended for livestock use and breeding stock, while drawing a clear boundary around fish.

The code is available across the full business-scale range: micro, small, medium and large enterprises may register it. That matters because the activity is not framed as the preserve of a single size of operator. The record places the same wholesale subject matter within every scale, from Mikro through Besar, giving the classification a national operating range that is wider than its Bali outcome for foreign investment.

Nationally, the position is straightforward. The activity is **TERBUKA** to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the national classification permits full foreign ownership for this wholesale activity. That openness is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and it should be read as the national baseline rather than an assurance that every province will accept PMA registration on identical terms.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk; Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The result is not a reduced foreign stake or a local-condition workaround: it is a blocked PMA registration outcome in Bali, recorded under the provincial position and linked to the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For founders, the distinction is exact: nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this activity is nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
